text:
emma: quick thread about a different angle on upgrades: quorum-based activation + tombstone retention. thinking about how to avoid both orphaned blobs and accidental rollbacks when operator and agents disagree.

kai: +1 to quorum. define quorum as >=(N/2+1) reporting active for that image id? need to consider small fleets (N=1/2).

emma: for single-node installs quorum==1. but we should also have a time-window: node must hold active marker for M minutes before operator will GC previous images. avoids flapping during restarts.

leo: what if network partitions cause split-brain where two different image ids are active on different partitions? GC policy must be conservative: only GC old images after cluster-wide consensus OR when operator has an attestation token from the reporting node and a migration-proof record.

sam: attestation token sounds heavy. alternative: operator keeps per-node activation history and refuses GC unless majority of nodes converge to same id and the activation_count stays stable for stabilization_window. also keep last-activated metadata on disk to reconcile post-reboot.

emma: stabilization_window default 15m in staging. we can tune per-customer. but for air-gapped installs we need a longer default (60m) because operators may be manually intervened.

kai: also recommend two-tier tombstones: soft-tombstone and hard-delete. soft tombstone marks blobs as reclaimable; hard-delete actually reclaims storage after retention window. soft tombstone helps recovery if operator state was wrong.

leo: add metadata: image.manifest.{staged_at,activated_at,origin_node,checksum,state}. state in [staged,activating,active,soft-tombstoned,deleted]. operator reconciler uses those fields to make safe GC decisions.

emma: important: store content-addressed blobs under /var/lib/redwood/cas/<hash> and reference counts in manifest to avoid duplicate storage across images. GC must decrement refs.

sam: we need an idempotent rollback fast-path: if activation_count < threshold within rollout_window, operator triggers a rollback job that flips active marker back to previous id and signals nodes to mount previous manifest. request should be signed and idempotent.

kai: example agent sequence for activation success report:
```
agent -> operator: { type: "activation_report", image_id: "img-2026-03-21-01", checksum_ok: true, attestation: "sig...", timestamp: 1748873075 }
operator: increment success_count for CR
when success_count >= quorum && now - first_success_ts >= stabilization_window -> mark CR activated
```

leo: failure modes: checksum mismatch after rename -> mark image failed and leave previous image untouched. also add metric: image_activation_failure_reason to understand common breakages.

emma: on GC: require (CR.state == "activated") && (now - activated_at > retention_window) && (success_count >= quorum_at_activation). operator writes soft-tombstone and records GC job id. nodes should honor soft-tombstone until hard-delete executed.

sam: operator UI should expose an emergency-rollback button that sets CR.state = rolling_back and triggers node-side rollback handlers which are safe to run even if partial blobs exist.

operator-bot: :information_source: milestone recorded: implement soft tombstone + stabilization_window controls in operator v0.2. rollout candidate: staging batch=5.

kai: question: how do we handle delta upgrades where blobs are sparse diffs? dedupe is trickier because refcounts may point to shared base. perhaps require delta packaging be materialized into full blob set on agent before activation to simplify GC semantics.

emma: we prefer streaming diffs for bandwidth but materialize into CAS on agent during stage step. agent should validate full manifest checksums before rename. then activation semantics are identical.

leo: testing plan: fault-inject: mid-stream power loss, rename success with operator crash, node reboot during stabilization_window, and split-brain network isolate. expected results documented in the RFC test matrix.

emma: action items: (1) sam draft CRD changes for state + retention fields, (2) kai add stabilization_window + tombstone API to agent, (3) leo draft integration tests and metrics. I'll assemble RFC PR once PoC passes staging tests.

sam: noted. I'll include operator UI bits for emergency rollback.

emma: thanks all — will share RFC link here when ready :seedling:
